title: Time-Resolved Spectral Micro-CT for Investigating Dynamic Processes in Pore Structures
content: Micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is a powerful, non-destructive imaging technique for characterizing the internal structure of geological samples at spatial scales ranging from centimeters to micrometers. Its non-invasive nature makes it particularly suitable for studying dynamic processes, enabling the visualization of geological material behavior under external influences such as temperature, pressure, and fluid interactions. Time-resolved (dynamic) micro-CT has been extensively applied to fluid flow studies, offering critical insights into pore-scale fluid dynamics. In the context of reactive fluid flow through complex geological materials, time-resolved micro-CT can localize chemical reactions within the pore space and identify associated mineralogical transformations.
